Raymond III Count of Tripoli was a member of the House of Châtillon and ruled as Count of Tripoli from 1147 until his death in 1178
He was the son of William II Count of Tripoli and Sybille of Jerusalem
Raymond III succeeded his father at a young age and became a ward of King Fulk of Jerusalem
**_*Early Life and Reign*_* 
Raymond III was taken captive by Nur ad-Din during the Battle of Inab in 1149 and was released after a ransom was paid
He played a crucial role in the Siege of Ascalon in 1153
Raymond III married Sybille daughter of King Amalric I of Jerusalem in 1175
The marriage was short-lived as Raymond III died in 1178
**_*Capture and Ransom*_* 
Raymond III was known for his involvement in the politics of the Kingdom of Jerusalem
He supported the claims of Sybille's half-brother Baldwin IV to the throne
Raymond III also played a key role in the Battle of Montgisard in 1177
**_*Later Life and Death*_* 
Raymond III died without an heir and the County of Tripoli passed to his nephew William of Châtillon
The exact date of Raymond III's death is not certain but it is believed to be in 1178
Raymond III's legacy is still debated among historians with some viewing him as a capable leader and others as a less effective ruler
His death marked the end of the Châtillon dynasty's rule over the County of Tripoli
